name: Barrenness
overview: Scripture presents barrenness as both a reproach and a condition subject to God's sovereign intervention, as seen in the lives of Sarai, Rebekah, and others. For example, Sarai was initially barren (Genesis 11:30), yet God promised to change her name to Sarah, signifying a divine purpose (Genesis 17:15). The Lord opened the wombs of those like Rebekah in response to prayer (Genesis 25:21) and healed others when Abraham interceded (Genesis 20:17-18). Barrenness is thus portrayed as a state that can be miraculously removed, highlighting God's power and mercy in fulfilling His promises.
